results.answer: For NordChemica, the 30-day target for actionable alerts per day is to reduce to 500 or fewer actionable alerts per day. Additionally, an immediate reduction promised within 7 days of deploying the suppression tuning bundle is a 70% reduction in actionable alerts compared to the baseline. These commitments are part of the remediation plan to address alert noise and satisfy procurement requirements during renewal negotiations [art_0a135c689c08, art_ffa7143fb822].

The NordChemica remediation plan proposes an EN-DEDUPE sliding-window setting of 5 minutes (300 seconds) with pattern-based grouping by service, host, and event type. Additionally, the per-host rate limit set for heartbeat-missing-v1 is 1 per minute. These settings are part of the suppression tuning bundle scheduled for delivery on 2026-03-22 to reduce noisy alerts and improve alert signal quality [art_ffa7143fb822].

The contractual financial remedy offered to NordChemica is a conditional 6% credit on the contract for the next year. This credit is tied to specific success metrics: reducing actionable alerts by 70% within 7 days and achieving 500 or fewer actionable alerts per day within 30 days after deployment of the suppression tuning bundle, measured against an agreed analytics baseline. If these targets are not met, the 6% credit will be applied as a financial concession. The credit and its conditions are to be legally approved and documented as part of the renewal negotiation. The baseline report to establish the starting point for these metrics is due by 2026-03-20 end of day, the suppression tuning bundle is planned for delivery by 2026-03-22, and a dry-run to validate changes is scheduled from 2026-03-23 to 2026-03-25 [art_ffa7143fb822, art_0a135c689c08]. 

Exact contractual wording or document reference for the credit clause is not provided in the evidence.

For Aurora University's Ontario campus, the temporary Signal Ingest transform (SI-ETL-FILTER) populates the field canonical.student_id by concatenating the region_code, a hyphen, and the local.student_number, but only if the event contains local.student_number and does not already have canonical.student_id. This mapping is non-destructive, preserving the original local.student_number field. Additionally, the transform adds a metadata field ingest.transform_version with the value "aurora-v1" to the event. This transform is scoped exclusively to the aurora tenant as a short-term fix pending migration to a central identity service within 6 weeks. The schema registry version is also bumped and registered with backward compatibility to record this change [art_db3975cc8475].

The rollback window for the Aurora Ontario production deploy is 60 minutes. The automatic safeguard that triggers a disable is if more than 2% message drop is observed during the deploy [art_db3975cc8475].

The mapping events failed primarily due to inconsistencies in SCIM mappings and approval chain variants across departments. Specifically, about 30% of failures were caused by the missing 'role' attribute in ServiceNow 'store' catalog webhooks, while the corporate catalog used a legacy key 'job_code' instead of 'role'. Additionally, occasional collector backfill caused delayed visibility. These issues led to approximately 9,000 failed mapping events out of 28,000 provisioning-related events between February 15 and March 3, 2026. The root cause was identified as SCIM mapping and approval chain inconsistencies and non-harmonized ServiceNow webhook variants across catalogs.

Northstar recommended a fix that involved immediately staging an ETL normalization filter (SI-ETL-FILTER) in a non-production environment starting March 19, 2026. This filter would map the legacy 'job_code' key to 'role', provide fallback heuristics, and tag all normalized events. They also recommended implementing an Orchestrator playbook to automatically retry store-catalog provisioning and perform dry-run re-triggers for the corporate catalog, including audit logs and safe rollback mechanisms. Furthermore, Northstar planned to build a Signal Insights dashboard to monitor provisioning latency and failed mapping counters and to modify the retention policy for provisioning logs to 365 days to support auditability. This remediation plan was approved on March 18, 2026, with a timeline for testing, deployment, and board reporting through mid-April 2026. [art_ab3362f35c1b, art_fceed52dcb35]

results.answer:
If validation checks fail during the live patch window for Verdant Bay (scheduled 2026-03-24 02:00-04:00 local), the system will automatically execute a rollback to the pre-patch ruleset. The rollback procedure involves running the command `orchestrator rollback --target ruleset=<prior_sha>`, which rehydrates the prior rules and triggers the cache invalidation hook to ensure system state consistency. After rollback, the team must notify Verdant Bay, open an incident for manual remediation, and revert any partial replays that may have occurred. This rollback is part of an atomic deployment process that includes draining worker pools incrementally, deploying the ruleset branch atomically, triggering cache invalidation, and running validation jobs on synthetic and in-flight approvals. Additionally, before patching, a pre-patch snapshot of OR-AUDIT-LOGS for the last 30 days is exported and saved to an evidence bucket as read-only to support audit and compliance needs [art_fff67d92fe41]. 

Detailed step-by-step instructions or scripts for executing the rollback command during the live patch window are not provided, nor are specific failure criteria beyond "if any validation fails." Timing or duration details beyond the command usage and post-rollback notifications are also not specified in the evidence.
